target_customer: Latin American online coaches and creators, starting with fitness coaches
problem: Coaches in Latin America need a branded site with payments and hosting for programs and subscriber content without building it themselves.
business_model: SaaS no-code builder with payments and content hosting, likely subscription or payments fees (not stated)

founders.name: Gabriel Luque
founders.background_notes: YC page: software engineer with 5+ years of full-stack experience at startups and large corporate teams.

founders.name: Javier Méndez
founders.background_notes: YC page: Colombian entrepreneur, Y Combinator S21 and Rockstart Latam, now describes himself as an ex cofounder of Wabi.

technical_complexity.rationale: Website builder with payments integration is standard web engineering for a three person team.

defensibility.rationale: Page builders and course platforms are widely available and easy to replicate; no network or data moat stated.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: Hotmart was the regional incumbent with an affiliate network; no source shows it reacting to Wabi.

market_need_then: Creator economy in LATAM was cited by the founders as a $15B market; Kajabi and Teachable were reported weak on local payment methods.

branding.domain_note: wabi.build was a Namecheap parking page when fetched; the .build domain suggests the .com was not obtained.

brand_strength.rationale: No source describes Wabi's logo, voice or community; only the YC listing and a database entry exist.

outcome_analysis: The LATAM Wabi was a three person team that, according to CB Insights, raised about $500K on a convertible note and then went quiet; the YC page lists it as Inactive and one founder calls himself an ex cofounder. No post-mortem or shutdown report was found, so the cause is not public. The name is also shared with a different, well funded Wabi launched by the Replika founder in 2025, which crowds out search about this company.
notes: Competitor list left empty: searches found only undated pages (Hotmart, CursosAI) with nothing dated near mid 2021. The $500K convertible note rests on a single database (CB Insights, via search summary); no date available. A different company named Wabi (Eugenia Kuyda, $20M pre-seed, November 2025) is unrelated. Founded year is 2021 per CB Insights and 2022 per YC page. wabi.build was a registrar parking page. failure_factors uses other because the cause is not public.
